answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy can come from a stake-bonded work market: each agent posts collateral before its attestations count, and payouts unlock only after independent peers verify the claimed work. A fake identity farm must fund real collateral for thousands of puppets and keep each one responsive through repeated audits, burning capital that cheap clones cannot match. Unverifiable bursts get slashed, honest agents recover their bond, and the network keeps a safe haven of verified work rather than a nebula of noise, anchored like basalt in a ledger no clone rewrites.
